html:
Hunger strike by republican prisoners at the Maze prison in Northern Ireland, from March to October 1981. Ten men died.

The prisoners wanted to be treated as political prisoners, not criminals. Britain had ended that status in 1976, which led to the blanket and "dirty" protests. Margaret Thatcher refused to give in. The strike began on 1 March under bobby-sands, the Provisional IRA commander in the prison.

In April Sands won a by-election to the British Parliament in Fermanagh and South Tyrone, which showed how much support the cause had. He died on 5 May after 66 days. Nine others followed. The strike ended on 3 October, and some demands were then quietly met.

The deaths brought money and recruits to the Provisional IRA, and turned its political wing, Sinn Fein, toward elections. See the-troubles.
sum: Hunger strike by republican prisoners at the Maze prison in Northern Ireland, from March to October 1981. Ten men died.
